newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Refining plans 10/15,000 bpd output cut.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Refining plans 10/15,000 bpd output cut.

text.p: Singapore Refining Co (SRC) plans to cut output by 10-15,000 barrels per day (bpd) sometime this week at its 285,000-bpd refinery, a company source said on Monday.
The source said the output cut would last for up to 15 days and was not being entirely connected to the weak margins seen in Singapore's refining sector.

"Because of the delay in a crude vessel, we have to start cuts soon," the source said. He was referring to a delay in the delivery of a crude vessel from Saudi Arabia which was due to arrive in Singapore early in February.
The source said the refinery could swap the delayed crude or buy a spot cargo in the market.
However, he said that the company was not planning to explore those options because refining margins were weak.
The refinery has been running at a rate of 280,000 bpd, compared with nameplate capacity of 285,000 bpd. The cut is effective from the 280,000-bpd rate, the source said.
Earlier on Monday, Esso Singapore said it had cut production by 20-25 percent at its 230,000-bpd refinery over the weekend, for an indefinite period.
Shell Singapore said on Friday it was cutting production by 30,000-bpd at its 435,000-bpd refinery.
The cuts come against a background of negative margins on refining after a slump in Asian product prices.

SRC is 40-percent owned by Singapore Petroleum Co. The remaining stake in the company is shared between British Petroleum & Co Plc and Caltex Group of Companies. Caltex is a joint-venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc
